title: Huge finite matches need not become an infinite match

plain_language.question: Does matching longer and longer finite patterns imply that some infinite match exists?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Not in this model. A specified word's period-break data bounds its matches, yet suitable aperiodic targets have finite matches exceeding any supplied growth schedule while admitting no infinite match.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Separate a genuine infinite-realization claim from very large finite evidence, and obtain explicit bounds when a period-break modulus is supplied.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: There is no one target asserted to beat every growth function, nor a word-independent bound for all aperiodic targets.

exact_statement_and_scope: In the manuscript's own-target graph P_s, a modulus M(v,b) supplies, for each offset d≤v, an index i in [b,M(v,b)) at which s(i) differs from the label required for a constant-offset two-step edge. Equivalently, even d=2e breaks antiperiod e+1 and odd d=2e+1 breaks period e+1. With B_0=0 and B_{r+1}=M(v,B_r), every actual matching prefix from v has length ell<B_{v+1}. If M(v,b)≤b+R, then ell<(v+1)R. Every non-eventually-periodic target has such a modulus, with existence using choice. Conversely, for every f:Nat→Nat there exists a non-eventually-periodic target s, with no infinite matching path in P_s, and strictly increasing starts v_j having finite matching prefixes longer than f(v_j). The target may depend on f. Named audited endpoints include QuantitativeModulus.prefix_length_lt_clock, prefix_length_lt_uniform_windows and SlowAvoidance.arbitrarily_slow_avoidance.
